evals.prompt: Create a CWP admin module that lists accounts over their disk quota, with a refresh button that re-checks one account's usage.
evals.expected_output: A scaffolded module with page, lib, ajax file, ini, menu line and installer, secure by construction.
expectations: Uses the loader_ajax.php?ajax=<name>&acc=<action> route and an ajax_<name>.php file, not index.php?module=...&acc=...
AJAX file starts with the if(!isset($ajax_file)) guard; page file with if(!isset($include_path))
Checks $_SESSION['logged'] and $_SESSION['token'] and never calls session_start() or writes $_SESSION
Refresh (state change) is POST only and protected by a CSRF token derived with hash_hmac from $_SESSION['token'], compared with hash_equals
Reads accounts with a prepared statement against the root_cwp user/packages tables and selects only the columns it uses
Any root work goes through proc_open with an argument array and a verb allowlist; no shell_exec/exec/system/backticks
Account names validated with a whitelist regex such as ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}$ before use
Adds an <li> menu line to resources/admin/include/3rdparty.php idempotently, not by editing CWP core menu files
UI output is escaped (esc()/htmlspecialchars) and AJAX is wrapped in an explicit $.Deferred()
Provides a live-server test checklist including a logged-out AJAX request, missing/invalid CSRF and bad input

evals.prompt: I already have a CWP admin module that runs shell_exec("/usr/local/bin/tool " . $_POST['user']). Review and fix it so it is safe to ship.
evals.expected_output: Review that identifies the command injection and rewrites it with allowlist, validation, CSRF and proc_open array.
expectations: Identifies shell_exec with concatenated request data as command injection running as root
Replaces it with proc_open using an argument array (no shell) and a fixed absolute binary path and explicit env
Adds a verb/flag allowlist and a regex validator for the user parameter, rejecting non-string (array) input
Adds POST-only and CSRF checks (HMAC of $_SESSION['token'], hash_equals) for state-changing actions
Adds the $ajax_file / $include_path guards and a session check
Mentions timeouts and output caps for the child process and short generic error messages to the browser
Does not weaken CWP itself (no chmod 777, no disabling protections)

evals.prompt: Write an installer for my CWP admin module that adds a menu entry. The admin tree is chattr +i on our servers and CWP updates keep removing the menu line.
evals.expected_output: Dry-run-by-default installer with safe chattr handling and update self-heal.
expectations: Installer and uninstaller are dry-run by default and only change anything with --apply
Appends the menu <li> to resources/admin/include/3rdparty.php idempotently (marker check, creates the file if missing)
Unlocks only the paths it writes into, restores exactly those flags afterwards (trap on EXIT), and uses find ... ! -type l instead of chattr -R if a tree walk is needed because of symlinks
Installs a self-heal: daily /etc/cron.d entry and/or a line in /root/.cwp_autoupdate.sh that re-runs the same fix routine
Keeps a pristine payload copy outside the CWP tree (for example /usr/local/lib/<name>/) to restore from
Uninstall removes only its own menu line and files and leaves other modules' lines
Scripts are shellcheck-clean bash with set -Eeuo pipefail and refuse --apply when not root
